To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

sS is a second vegetative s factor with a major role in cell physiology, that the sS dependent regulon can be subdivided into a number of modules, that the architecture of these modules is subject to regulatory control, that the s70 RNA polymerases are subject to extensive regulatory control by other global regulators, and that the sS consensus promoter can be identified in silico.

(1) up to 10 % of E. coli genes can be directly or indirectly controlled by sS (or the RpoS sigma factor) (2) the sS consensus promoter can be predicted in silico (3) sS should be viewed as a second vegetative (nonstress specific) sigma factor and (4) the sS dependent network exhibits regulatory overlaps with other regulatory networks.

(i) sS is the master regulator for the general stress response, (ii) sS is a second major sigma factor with a large impact on E. coli cell physiology, (iii) the sS dependent regulon is highly complex and consists of several regulatory networks that are controlled by sS and other global regulators, (iv) the sS regulon is a regulatory network with extensive overlaps with other regulons.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the global transcriptional regulatory network that governs the expression of stress resistance genes in E. coli and the identification of its key regulatory elements and control points.
the analysis of the sS (RpoS) dependent general stress response network in Escherichica coli and its regulation.
the identification, characterization, and analysis of the general stress regulon of Escherichia Coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sS and s70 RNA polymerases act together in an intricate regulatory network that controls a large number of genes in response to a variety of environmental conditions and that this network can be modulated by additional regulators.
the general stress response network is highly dynamic, and that it can be modified by the cell in order to respond to specific environmental challenges.
the sS regulon is a network of networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sS dependent gene expression is controlled by a complex regulatory network that can be temporarily modified to adapt to specific growth conditions.
the sS dependent network is a major regulatory hub for the global stress response in E. coli.
the general stress response network is not only a major regulatory network but also a major architectural component of the global E. coli regulons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single sigma factor (sS) is able to control a complex network of genes and gene expression modules.

sS is a major player in the control of cell physiology in response to a wide variety of stress signals and that the sS dependent regulatory network is a complex regulatory system with multiple levels of control.

the general stress response is a major component of E. coli physiology under nonoptimum growth conditions and that sS dependent transcriptional control represents a major regulatory mechanism for adaptation to a broad range of stress conditions.
